newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends weaker, further losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends weaker, further losses seen.

text.p: FORECAST RANGE 1.3850/1.3900 ASIAN CLOSE 1.3812
RESISTANCE 1.3800 SUPPORT 1.3950 HI 1.3836 LO 1.3807
CANADA OPEN 1.3835/40 HI 1.3865 EUROPE OPEN 1.3802
* Canada's dollar ended weaker around C$1.3875 (US$0.7207) on
Wednesday from Tuesday's close at C$1.3800 (US$0.7246).
* Further weakness expected overnight with a possible move to
C$1.3900 level, traders said.
* Earlier break through key C$1.3845-50 level triggered
stop-loss orders on International Money Market.
"We're looking at a very negative close at these levels. We
may see some weakness toward C$1.3900 (overnight)," another
trader said.
The unit was expected to favor the weak side of its trading
range as the market awaited Canada's July labor force data due
on Friday.
Canada's July unemployment rate was forecast to ease to
9.08 percent from 9.1 percent in June, according to a Reuters
survey of economists.
In other news, Bank of Montreal on Wednesday predicted
Canada would see strong economic growth in 1997 and 1998.
In its mid-year economic review, Canada's third largest bank forecast Canadian economic growth of 3.5 percent in 1997 and 3.7 percent in 1998.
The bank predicted the Canadian dollar would appreciate through the rest of 1997 and 1998, although it would remain undervalued and continue to be supportive of Canadian exporters.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar slipped to 85.42 Japanese yen from Tuesday's close of 85.69, but climbed to 1.3551 marks from Tuesday's 1.3479 marks.
((Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100))
